transcript:
[00:00] Samira (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Priya (GreenLeaf): Priya here, Head of Data. Marcus on video, Dr. Voss and Omar also here.
[00:12] Marcus: Morning.
[00:15] Samira: Awesome. Diego and Lena from our SE team are on as well. Goal today is to align on the quality evaluation plan for the POC — golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination/format checks, scoring approach, and timeline.
[00:30] Diego (Redwood SE): Quick context, we'll run two buckets: 1) functional quality evals — correctness/clinical fidelity, hallucination checks, format conformance; 2) performance/ops — latency p50/p95, throughput, cost per 1k tokens. We'll stitch results into a scoring rubric.
[00:45] Priya: Sounds good. For success criteria, from our side we need: zero high-severity hallucinations on the golden set, >90% format adherence for structured outputs, and average response time p95 < 800ms for our 256-token median use case. Also cost needs to be within our projected budget, but quality trumps cost for initial pilot.
[01:05] Diego: Noted. When you say zero high-severity hallucinations, can you define high-severity?
[01:10] Dr. Voss: High-severity = any generated clinical recommendation or wrong medication/dosage that could change care. Low-severity would be minor phrasing or non-actionable extra text.
[01:22] Lena: We'll build a manual adjudication for the golden prompts plus an automated hallucination detector that flags unsupported facts. The adjudication will be by your clinical SMEs — we'll provide a CSV with model outputs side-by-side.
[01:35] Marcus: For workload sizing, our expected production peak is about 40 requests per second across our API, but the POC realistic test dataset will be much smaller — around 5000 requests/day with bursts to 200 rps for short windows. Typical sequence length distribution: 40% short (<=64 tokens), 50% medium (65-256), 10% long (257-1024).
[02:00] Diego: Great, that distribution helps pick batching and kernel configs. For the benchmark we'll emulate that distribution and run a steady-state throughput test (30 minutes) and a burst test (5 minutes at 200 rps).
[02:12] Omar (GreenLeaf): Network: we need to know whether the benchmark requires inbound firewall exceptions or if you can run from a hosted sandbox. We prefer VPC/private for PHI.
[02:22] Samira: For the initial quality eval (text-only golden prompts and regression), we can run on our hosted environment without PHI, using synthetic or redacted samples. For later performance benchmarks with real-ish traffic we can schedule a Dedicated run or a Private deployment trial. We'll share options with estimated costs.
[02:40] Priya: On the golden prompts: we will provide 20-30 high-value prompts covering extraction, summarization, and triage. We also want edge-case prompts to surface hallucinations. How do you propose we score those?
[02:55] Diego: Proposed scoring approach — keep it simple and weighted: accuracy/clinical correctness 50%, hallucination rate 25% (lower is better), format adherence 15%, and latency/ops 10% (for the POC quality gate we can treat latency more as a gating metric than a score). We'll compute a weighted score per prompt and aggregate to a final pass/fail threshold — suggested pass threshold 85/100.
[03:20] Priya: 85 sounds reasonable as a starting point. For hallucination detection, do you rely on automated heuristics or human review?
[03:28] Lena: Both. We'll run automated heuristics for obvious entity mismatches, unsupported facts, and hallucination classifiers; every flagged output will be reviewed by a clinician for the golden set. For regression tests we'll run automated checks first, then sample failures for human review.
[03:42] Marcus: Regression tests — we have an existing baseline from an internal finetuned model. We want to ensure no degradation vs baseline on intent/tasks. What's your plan to compare?
[03:52] Diego: We'll take your baseline model outputs for the same prompt set and compute relative delta on the main metrics (accuracy, hallucination rate, format adherence). The POC will include a regression suite of ~1,000 prompts covering high-frequency intents — that'll be automated.
[04:05] Priya: For scoring, can we get a per-intent breakdown? Some intents (medication reconciliation) are higher weight than general triage.
[04:12] Samira: Absolutely — weightings per intent can be configured. We'll work with Priya to assign criticality weights. That will flow into the aggregated score.
[04:20] Dr. Voss: Also we need a hallucination taxonomy in the report: critical clinical halluc, minor factual mismatch, hallucination of nonexistent source, and format corruption.
[04:32] Diego: We'll include that taxonomy and map detection outcomes to severity.
[04:36] Marcus: On formatting checks, outputs must match JSON schema when present. If model generates extra commentary, it should be captured separately. How tolerant are you of trailing text?
[04:46] Lena: We'll run strict schema validation as a gating test — pass/fail — and also compute a graded metric for partial conformance. For POC acceptance, we suggest 90% strict schema pass.
[04:55] Priya: Benchmarks and timelines?
[05:00] Samira: Proposed timeline: this week (by 2026-07-17) greenleaf shares golden prompts and dataset samples. Redwood will provide the security pack and benchmark repo same week. Benchmark run planned for week of 2026-07-20 (30-minute steady-state + burst tests + quality eval on golden set). Results and report by 2026-07-24. Then 6-week pilot to follow if pass.
[05:20] Omar: For the performance runs that simulate PHI, we need to do that on Dedicated or Private. What's the minimum Dedicated capacity you'd recommend for your p95 < 800ms target?
[05:30] Diego: Initial estimate: for your distribution and target 200 rps bursts, two A100-ish instances with continuous batching should achieve the p95 target — but we'll validate in the benchmark. We'll include cost estimates in the pack.
[05:42] Marcus: What about caching or prefix KV cache — will that skew the numbers?
[05:47] Diego: We'll control for caching: run cold-start and warm-start tests. Part of the ops bench will be KV/prefix cache enabled vs disabled to show delta in tokens/sec and cost.
[05:58] Priya: Can the scoring harness run in our environment? We want reproducibility.
[06:03] Lena: Yes, we'll deliver a Dockerized harness and instructions. You can run it locally; we can also run from Redwood infra and share reproducible logs.
[06:12] Dr. Voss: For the clinical adjudication, we'll need an exportable format and a simple UI to mark issues.
[06:18] Samira: We'll provide a CSV and a lightweight review UI — reviewers can flag outputs with severity and notes.
[06:24] Marcus: How will you measure hallucination rate quantitatively?
[06:28] Diego: We'll report hallucination rate as percentage of outputs with at least one critical hallucination, and also a normalized hallucination severity score (e.g., critical=3, moderate=2, minor=1) averaged across prompts. That becomes the hallucination component in the weighted score.
[06:45] Priya: Any recommended pass/fail thresholds for the regression suite?
[06:49] Diego: For regression: no more than a 2% absolute drop in accuracy vs baseline on prioritized intents, and no more than a 1% increase in critical hallucinations. These are negotiable but are reasonable starting gates.
[06:59] Samira: To recap next steps and artifacts: greenleaf shares prompts and samples by 7/17; Redwood shares security docs and harness by 7/17; Diego publishes benchmark script by 7/20; schedule run week of 7/20. Report out on 7/24.
[07:15] Priya: Ok. We'll need the SOC2 and SSP up front for our security review.
[07:20] Samira: We'll email that today.
[07:23] Marcus: Last question — how do you handle versioning and rollbacks in case of quality regressions during pilot?
[07:29] Lena: Redwood supports pinning model versions and automatic fallback policies; in Dedicated you can configure canary rollouts and automatic rollback on metric degradation. We'll include a suggested rollout policy.
[07:41] Dr. Voss: Thanks, that addresses concerns.
[07:43] Samira: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts and calendar invites for the bench.
[07:48] Priya: Thanks all.
[07:50] End of call.

Notes: Transcript has some auto-transcription noise; speaker labels were edited for clarity. Outputs of benchmark will include CSV exports: prompt, baseline_output, redwood_output, accuracy, hallucination_flag, severity, latency_ms.

Quality eval plan (summary):
- Golden prompts: 20-30 clinician-curated prompts covering high-value workflows + 10 edge cases. Human adjudication + automated heuristics.
- Regression suite: ~1,000 prompts covering top intents; automated scoring vs your baseline (accuracy + hallucination delta).
- Hallucination checks: automated classifier + human review; severity taxonomy; report hallucination rate and severity-weighted score.
- Format checks: strict JSON/schema validation gating for structured outputs (target >=90%); graded metric for partial conformance.
- Scoring approach: weighted aggregate 0-100: accuracy 50, hallucination (inverse) 25, format adherence 15, ops/latency 10. Pass threshold proposed >=85. Intent-level weights configurable.
- Benchmarks: steady-state throughput (30m), burst test (5m at 200 rps), cold vs warm cache runs. Metrics: p50/p95 latency, req/sec, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens.
- Timeline: asset exchange by 2026-07-17; benchmark run week of 2026-07-20; results by 2026-07-24; 6-week pilot to follow on success.

Final recap and next steps in calendar invite and action_items list above.
